title: Three reasons why hiring frontline workers takes 14+ days
summary: Cut frontline hiring time in half with verified candidates who show up. Solve the resume overload, interview no-shows, and high turnover challenges.
body_markdown:
Most managers and recruiters know the frustration. Filling frontline roles shouldn’t take weeks, but for many businesses it drags on for more than 14 days. Why?


‍


There are three consistent reasons we hear from Partners:


1. Too many resumes, too few skills: 70% of employers say they struggle to find qualified candidates from the massive amounts of resumes coming in from job boards. Hours get wasted searching for the right fit.
2. Interview no-shows: In hospitality, 57% of candidates don’t show up to the interview. In warehousing, it’s up to 30%. Recruiters end up doubling interview schedules, only to lose time on candidates who were never serious.
3. High attrition: With a 75% turnover among hourly workers, managers are stuck backfilling instead of moving operations forward.


‍


The result? Overstuffed funnels, lost recruiter hours, and managers pulled away from running the business.


‍


But it doesn’t have to be this way. Instawork Hiring starts with verified candidates who show up, cutting time-to-fill by nearly half. That means:


✅ Faster offers, so you don’t lose talent to competitors


✅ Reliable hires who keep operations steady


✅ Managers who can focus on growth instead of constant backfilling


‍


When a high school food service operation struggled to fill a Cashier position, they posted an interview shift with Instawork. They conducted three interviews on Wednesday, and by the next day, they were ready to send an offer to a candidate. This shows how quickly you can make quality hires with our approach.
